clinicalPearls: Caused by variants in FHL1 on the X chromosome, encoding the four-and-a-half LIM domain protein 1; inheritance is X-linked so males are typically more severely affected than heterozygous females
Presents with progressive proximal and axial weakness, and rigid spine or scoliosis can be prominent features
The clinical spectrum ranges from severe early-childhood-onset disease to milder later-onset forms
Cardiac involvement and respiratory muscle weakness can occur, given FHL1 expression in cardiac and skeletal muscle, so cardiorespiratory surveillance is important

The defining biopsy feature is reducing bodies, cytoplasmic inclusions that stain intensely with menadione-linked nitro-blue tetrazithium (menadione-NBT) in the absence of substrate, reflecting their reducing activity
Reducing bodies contain aggregated mutant FHL1 protein and can be confirmed with FHL1 immunostaining and electron microscopy
Creatine kinase is normal to moderately elevated and electromyography shows myopathic, sometimes irritable, changes
Diagnosis combines the reducing-body biopsy finding with FHL1 genetic testing
reference.pathophysiology: Reducing body myopathy is caused by variants in FHL1, an X-linked gene encoding a LIM-domain protein involved in sarcomere assembly, mechanotransduction, and cytoskeletal signalling in striated muscle. Disease-associated variants, frequently affecting the zinc-coordinating residues of the second LIM domain, cause the mutant protein to misfold and self-aggregate. These aggregates form the characteristic reducing bodies, which have intrinsic reducing activity demonstrable with the menadione-NBT reaction, and their accumulation is toxic to muscle fibres, producing progressive weakness. Because FHL1 is also expressed in cardiac muscle, some patients develop cardiomyopathy.
additionalDifferentials: Other FHL1-related myopathies (X-linked myopathy with postural muscle atrophy, scapuloperoneal myopathy, Emery-Dreifuss-like phenotype)
Congenital myopathies with cores or aggregates
Rigid spine syndrome from SELENON-related myopathy
additionalInvestigations: Muscle biopsy with the menadione-NBT reaction, FHL1 immunostaining, and electron microscopy to demonstrate reducing bodies
Muscle MRI to define involvement, including paraspinal muscles
Cardiac evaluation and respiratory function testing
redFlags: Cardiomyopathy or conduction abnormality on cardiac assessment
Respiratory muscle weakness or nocturnal hypoventilation
Rapidly progressive weakness or severe early-onset disease
Progressive rigid spine or scoliosis compromising respiration
reference.prognosis: Prognosis varies with age of onset and sex: severe early-onset disease in males can progress rapidly with loss of ambulation and significant cardiorespiratory involvement, whereas later-onset and female cases may follow a milder course; cardiac and respiratory complications are important determinants of outcome.
pitfalls: Missing reducing bodies unless the menadione-NBT reaction is specifically performed on the biopsy
Neglecting cardiac and respiratory surveillance given the FHL1 gene's cardiac role
Failing to recognise the X-linked inheritance pattern and its counselling implications
Confusing the inclusions with other cytoplasmic bodies without confirmatory staining
references: Bradley and Daroff Neurology in Clinical Practice
management: No disease-specific drug therapy exists, so care is supportive and multidisciplinary around the progressive muscle weakness
Physiotherapy and occupational therapy to maintain function and mobility, with orthoses and assistive devices
Orthopaedic management of rigid spine and scoliosis, including bracing and corrective spinal surgery
Cardiac surveillance with echocardiography and ECG for cardiomyopathy and conduction disease, given FHL1 expression in cardiac muscle
Respiratory monitoring with lung-function testing and non-invasive ventilation for respiratory muscle weakness
Genetic counselling for this X-linked disorder with carrier testing of female relatives, escalating to specialist neuromuscular and cardiorespiratory services on deterioration
